entities.name: Query MurD ligase
observations: 493 aa protein; predicted molecular mass 54.7 kDa and theoretical pI 8.02.
Strong homology to reviewed bacterial UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanyl-D-glutamate--2,6-diaminopimelate ligases: 56.9–58.5% identity, 98.6–99.4% query coverage, E-values 2.7e-199 to 5.4e-201.
Pfam domains support the MurD family: Mur_ligase PF01225 at residues 29–94, Mur_ligase_M PF08245 at 106–311, and Mur_ligase_C PF02875 at 334–459.
Reference homologs annotate ATP binding, Mg2+ binding, cytoplasmic localization, and peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
A conserved N6-carboxylysine modification is annotated in homologs; the query position is not experimentally mapped by this analysis.
Exact organism and substrate specificity are inferred from homologs rather than directly experimentally established for this sequence.

entities.name: MurD ligase reaction
observations: Reaction corresponds to EC 6.3.2.13 and Rhea RHEA:23676 in reviewed homolog annotations.
The enzyme is an ATP-dependent ligase that adds meso-diaminopimelate to the UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala-D-Glu precursor during bacterial peptidoglycan biosynthesis.

entities.name: MurD Mg2+ dependence
observations: Reviewed homologs annotate Mg2+ as a cofactor and magnesium-ion binding as a molecular function; ATP binding is also annotated.

entities.name: Peptidoglycan biosynthesis
observations: MurD ligase activity occurs in bacterial cell-wall peptidoglycan biosynthesis and supports cell division and cell-shape regulation.
